webpage.text:
United Airlines Basic Economy Review: What Is It Like To Fly United Basic Economy?

United Dulles Airport picture by Tracy Nicole

I fly basic economy almost every month to save money. I was going to New York City for the holidays in December. United’s basic economy was the best deal, so I flew it.

In general, basic economy will save you around $70-$100 when flying on a domestic round trip flight, and around $200 when flying on an international one.

I fly to different cities every month, so basic economy savings matter to me. It is money toward the cost of my next flight.

I said I would review the Big 3 carriers on an actual basic economy flights, so you can see what it is like. I did the Delta basic economy review as well as the American basic economy review. So, here is the United review.

This is what you can expect on a United basic economy flight.

The major carriers have basic economy to compete with low cost carriers (or so they say). Basic economy is not a separate section of the plane. It is more about restrictions like not getting to choose your seat for free or the inability to change your ticket.

Airlines don’t want you to fly basic economy. They want you to pay more for regular economy.

Honestly, each of the Big 3 airlines has positives and negatives when it comes to basic economy.

Here is a summary of the positives and negatives of each:

United Airlines

Positives:

 * earn miles with a credit card
 * get IFE (in flight entertainment) screen on most planes

Negatives:

 * not allowed free carry on (only personal item)
 * board in last group

American Airlines

Positives:

 * Allowed a free carry on
 * board early in group 6 if AAdvantage member
 * can possibly upgrade to First Class

Negatives:

 * don’t earn miles
 * no IFE screens yet

Delta Airlines

Positives:

 * get to choose seat for free during 24 check in
 * allowed free carry on
 * get IFE screens on most planes

Negatives:

 * don’t earn miles
 * board in last group
 * not allowed upgrade to first class or extra legroom seating

Not sure if basic economy is for you? Here is a post to explain the positives and negatives of flying basic economy.

RELATED: Should You Fly Basic Economy and Save Money


The Flight: Chicago To Newark

On December 16,2025 I flew from Chicago to Newark.

My home airport is Huntsvile Alabama. To fly to most cities, I usually have to connect through a big hub.

As an AvGeek, this is fun for me. I have fun exploring the big airport hubs around the country like Chicago, Los Angeles, Atlanta, Washington, D.C., and Dallas.

When flying Delta, I usually connect in Atlanta. When flying American, I usually connect in Charlotte, Chicago, or Dallas. This United connection was in Chicago.

On the flight home, the connection was through Washington, D.C. Dulles. I got to ride that weird people mover at Dulles.

So, my itinerary was:

 * Huntsville to Chicago
 * Chicago to Newark
 * Newark to Washington, D.C. Dulles
 * Washington D.C. Dulles (IAD) to Huntsville


How I Booked My Flight

I booked my flight with cash. Because it was a last minute trip to New York City for the holidays, I couldn’t find a normal priced flight to JFK or LaGuardia.

I could have gotten a flight to JFK, but I waited one day, and the price went up. I knew better, I just did it anyway.

I take public transportation from airports in the U.S.

Though JFK and LaGuardia can be easier to get to Manhattan on public transportation, it has been a while since I have flown through Newark, so it was actually ok

I have fun going through different hubs throughout the country again. I will need to get back to New York City in a couple months, so I will make sure to fly through JFK.

I have not flown out of JFK in a while,. My last trip to New York in 2023 was through LaGuardia. I plan to fly to New York City more anyway later (at least a couple times a year).

This is where points and miles come in handy. They really do allow you to travel more. I fly to other cities like Los Angeles, Chicago, and Vegas every year.

I paid cash for this flight again. When flying every month, I like to keep my flights around $250 which is why I fly mostly basic economy as I said earlier.

My city is more expensive than most. Flights out of bigger cities can be around $150 round trip. The $250 I paid is as cheap as it gets from my expensive airport. Later, I may drive to Nashville which is only an hour and a half to get cheaper flights.

My monthly flights are mostly cash right now. In the future, they will be with mostly miles though.

That is good on United because when using miles there is no such thing as basic economy. When using miles you are put in regular economy.

The same is true on American. Unfortunately, Delta has basic economy with miles, so you would need more miles to fly Delta regular economy.

Points and miles can really save you money, and get you to your next free flight, hotel, or entire trip quicker. You can find out how to get your first free trip with points and miles if you are a new to points and miles.


How I Choose My Basic Economy Seat

Of the four segments, I paid $20 to choose my seat on the Chicago to Newark flight. The other segments, I did not pay extra for seats, so they were selected by United,

Be careful when paying for seats with basic economy. You can defeat your savings.

United has an upsell as soon as you buy your ticket. It gives you regular economy features for more money and less perks. Don’t buy this. They will charge you higher than regular economy.

You can purchase individual seats on United for a decent price, usually around $20. Again watch out to not defeat your basic economy savings though.

So, what seats did I get on the other segments that I do not pay for?

This is where basic economy fliers end up in a middle seat. You don’t have to end up in a middle seat all the time though.

Because two of my flight segments were on regional jets, I didn’t get a middle seat because smaller planes have no middle seat.

I ended up in the dreaded middle seat from Newark to Washington though. Keep in mind that I could have ended up in a middle seat on the Chicago to Newark segment too if I had not paid the extra $20.

To me, this is one advantage Delta has over both United and American. On Delta, you can chose your seat for free 24 hours before check in.

It is still a gamble. If the flight is full, you will be assigned a seat by Delta,. That means you will probably end up in a middle seat.

However, when the flight is not full, you can get some good seats. I have even gotten rows to myself. I rarely end up in a middle seat on Delta. That could be just my experience though.

Honestly, most flights in the United States are short, so it is not the end of the world to end up in a middle seat. I have even been fine flying across the country from California to Washington DC in a middle seat in the past.

So my seats were:

 * Huntsville to Chicago -aisle seat (free)
 * Chicago to Newark – window seat (paid $20)
 * Newark to Washington Dulles – middle seat (free)
 * Washington Dulles to Huntsville – aisle seat (free)

RELATED: Choose Your Seat For Free With Delta Basic Economy


Boarding With Basic Economy

I was in the last boarding group on United. United and Delta both make people board in the last group when flying basic economy.

This is where American has the advantage as long as you are loyalty member. American let’s basic economy fliers board in group 6 instead of the last boarding group (group 9) if you are a loyalty member.

So, I boarded in group 6 on this United flight. This is the last boarding group on United.

RELATED: Board Early In American Airlines Basic Economy


The Onboard Experience

The onboard experience in basic economy is pretty much the same as regular economy after seat selection, and not being able to change your ticket.

Those are the two big restrictions that make basic economy a big deal on all three carriers. You could end up in dreaded middle seat. You also cannot change your ticket unless you pay a fee.

United like Delta has IFE (in flight entertainment) screens on most planes.

You only get a snacks on all the major carriers

I did end up in one middle seat again. I paid $20 for one segment which was the only other segment that could have been a middle seat. I paid because I cared about the view from Chicago to Newark.

Honestly, I fly United basic economy less than the other two carriers though.

Why?

United is still the only airline that does not let basic economy fliers bring a free carry on. This means that I bring my backpack on United like on a discount carrier.

I prefer to travel with a full carry on, so again United is my last choice. This is a big negative, and I think should change.

If this ever changed, I would fly United basic economy more because it is not a bad experience other than not being allowed a free carry on. For this review, I had a trip that was ok with a backpack, so I thought it would be an opportunity to write this review.


Summary

On December 16, 2025, I flew to Newark on United Airlines to enjoy the Christmas holidays in New York. I had a good time.

I have not been to New York during the holidays in a long time. I lived in New York City for almost decade when I was younger.

I will make the holidays a yearly trip to New York in December. Again, I plan to fly to New York more often too. I used to visit New York at least three times a year just to see friends

With points and miles, it is easy to fly to New York and other cities once a year or more. I usually fly to Chicago, L.A., Vegas, and Miami every year again.

That is the beauty of points and miles. So, make sure to see how to get your first free trip with points.

I hope you know what to expect on a United basic economy flight after reading this post.

As usual, if this review was helpful, share it below on social media.

ICE agents spotted at Reagan, still headed to Dulles

ICE agents spotted at Reagan National, still expected at Dulles

WASHINGTON - ICE agents were spotted at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport Monday evening and are reportedly headed to Dulles International Airport, where they will assist TSA with staffing shortages and long security lines, Fox News reported.


Trump deploys ICE to ease airport security lines

What they're saying:

Agents will be covering exits currently monitored by TSA agents, checking identification before people enter screening areas and assisting with crowd control and line management, per White House border czar Tom Homan, who was named by President Donald Trump to lead this effort. 

The president said over the weekend he would use federal immigration officers to help field long airport security lines starting Monday unless Democrats agreed on a bill to fund the Department of Homeland Security, and this morning, he did just that, deploying agents to over a dozen airports nationwide. 

(Photo by Sha Hanting/China News Service/VCG via Getty Images)

Reuters, CNN and The Associated Press were reporting ICE agents had been deployed to at least 13 major-city airports, based on information from sources, social media posts and first-hand reporter accounts: 

 * Chicago
 * Cleveland
 * Atlanta
 * Houston
 * New York (JFK and LaGuardia)
 * New Orleans
 * San Juan
 * New Jersey
 * Philadelphia
 * Phoenix
 * Pittsburgh
 * Fort Meyers

What you can do:

If you are traveling soon, check for updates from your local airport about its recommendation for arrival times. You can check their social media accounts or directly on the airport’s website. 

Also look for information from the airport you’re flying home from. Some major airports allow you to book a specific time slot for TSA security, which could help reduce wait times. 

The Source: Information was sourced from Tom Homan and President Donald Trump, along with reporting from Reuters and CNN. Background details were sourced from FOX Business, The Associated Press and prior FOX Television Stations coverage, with additional reporting by Megan Ziegler with FOX Local.

You can check their social media accounts or directly on the airport’s website. Also look for information from the airport you’re flying home from. Some major airports allow you to book a specific time slot for TSA security, which could help reduce wait times.

resultats_lens.texte_contexte: Des agents de l'ICE ont été aperçus à l'aéroport national Ronald Reagan de Washington lundi soir et sont attendus à l'aéroport international de Dulles pour assister la TSA face aux pénuries de personnel et aux longues files d'attente pour la sécurité. Cette mesure fait suite au déploiement par le président Donald Trump d'officiers fédéraux de l'immigration dans plus d'une douzaine d'aéroports à travers le pays. Les agents contrôlent les pièces d'identité et gèrent les foules. Le déploiement concerne également des aéroports à Chicago, Cleveland, Atlanta, Houston, New York (JFK et LaGuardia), New Orleans, San Juan, New Jersey, Philadelphia, Phoenix, Pittsburgh et Fort Myers.
